t: This is the Cheltenham Estate, an architectural complex in Kensington and Chelsea. It was designed by Ernő Goldfinger, the Hungarian-British architect and furniture designer, who lived from 1902 to 1987. I don't have more detail on its history, so I'll leave it there. What you can do is look at the estate as a piece of planned modern housing, shaped by an architect best known for his modernist approach.
